text:
irene: Heads up — new hire reported onboarding failure: Node/tsc fine, but Deno + esbuild in the edge sample both break.
noah: what breakage?
irene: Deno import fails with `Uncaught TypeError: Module "file:///.../redwood-inference/mod.ts" has no exported member 'createClient'`. esbuild bundling silently resolves to a CJS stub and named exports are missing. Also TS in the sandbox couldn't locate declarations.
tara: Did we try replicating with `npm pack` + tiny consumer? Deno uses ESM entry lookups differently and may prefer plain .ts/.mjs files.
pkg-bot: publish: detected package change  new `exports` added in last publish (refs: pkg@v3.2.1).
marco: I dug into the published tarball: package.json `exports` root is `{ "default": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "node": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./types/index.d.ts" }` and there's an `./deno` subpath that points to `./dist/esm/deno.mjs` but it's missing a `types` entry. There's also an upstream `types` field missing at top-level.
ivy: That combination explains a lot. Deno attempts to import the bare specifier and some importers prefer `./deno` or defaulting logic depending on the runtime. If the default is CJS, that won't work. And TypeScript won't find types if the top-level `types` is missing or exports don't include `types` for the root.
noah: Also esbuild (used by the sample bundler) prefers `import`/`module` conditions over `default` in some setups, but if our `exports` only exposes CJS as default and ESM under a special `deno` subpath, esbuild's resolver may still end up with the wrong file.
tara: Repro steps I ran:
```
# simulate consumer
mkdir /tmp/rwd-test && cd /tmp/rwd-test
npm pack ../redwood-inference && tar -xzf redwood-inference-3.2.1.tgz
# try requiring the package
node -e "console.log(require('./package/package.json').exports)"
# try import in Deno
deno run --allow-read ./package/dist/esm/deno.mjs
```
Denos run reported missing export.
marco: Short-term mitigation I pushed to the onboarding sample: changed imports to `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'` and updated the sample's bundler config to force ESM resolution. That unblocks the new hire but is ugly.
irene: We need a robust package.json layout that works for Node (CJS + ESM), Deno, bundlers (esbuild/vite), and TS consumers. Proposal:
- Add a top-level "types": "./types/index.d.ts" so TS always picks it up.
- Rework `exports` to include clear conditions: `import`, `require`, `node`, `deno`, `worker`, and `default` fallbacks. Also include `types` at the root and for each subpath.
- Add `module` -> ESM entry and `main` -> CJS entry for legacy resolvers.
- For Deno, include a `./deno` subpath and make sure it's a pure ESM file without CJS shims. Example:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./types/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "node": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "deno": "./dist/esm/deno.mjs",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./deno": {
    "types": "./types/deno.d.ts",
    "default": "./dist/esm/deno.mjs"
  }
}
```
ivy: I'd add `typesVersions` as a fallback for older TS that don't look at `exports.types`. Also include a `files` array and `prepack` to avoid shipping internal cjs artifacts that editors auto-import. That prevents VSCode from suggesting deep '/dist/cjs' paths.
noah: CI additions:
- pack-smoke-test that `npm pack` and runs a small Node ESM runner, a Node CJS require, and a Deno import of the packed files.
- run esbuild + vite build against the packed tarball to simulate browser bundlers.
- tsc --noEmit on a sample workspace to ensure types visible.
marco: I'll open a PR that adds the top-level `types`, expands `exports` with `types` in root and deno subpath, adds `module`/`main`, and updates `files` + `prepack` to strip internal trees.
tara: Can we also add a small README note in the samples about Deno and bundler quirks and a troubleshooting checklist: `npm pack` inspect, `node -e require.resolve('redwood-inference')`, `deno run ./package/dist/esm/deno.mjs`? That helps new hires debug faster.
irene: Good. Marco, please include a regression test in CI for Deno + esbuild. And please add a short blurb to release notes explaining the change so customers using Deno or esbuild know what to expect.
ivy: One more gotcha: some bundlers look for a `browser` field; we should avoid conflicting signals. Keep the exports authoritative and use `browser` only if we see consistent consumer issues in browser-only bundlers.
noah: Filed issue #8001 with links to the sample patch and the proposed package.json snippet. New hire is unblocked by the sample hack. We'll revert after the PR lands.
tara: Thanks all. Let's make the package layout explicit so Deno/esbuild/Node/TS all get the right thing without hacks. :thumbsup:
